IIMP 2000.title: Academic and Professional Development
IIMP 2000.description: This course is designed to assist students in developing attributes necessary for professional growth throughout their studies in the IIM program. It will also provide academic advising to students, to enhance their job hunting skills and, to improve their communication skills. Students are required to attend discussion sessions with advisors and selected workshops. For IIM students only. Graded P/PP/F.
cilos: Develop soft skills required for their academic and professional development.
Learn the academic and professional skills related to their career or academy study advancement.
Appreciate the need for soft skills in their professional development.

IIMP 4970.title: Interdisciplinary Industrial Project
IIMP 4970.description: Students in this project will be engaged in practical hands-on training for a period of at least 6 months, in a form of a full-time or part-time internship or co-op program in  an organization or company relevant to the students’ area of interest. Students are required to complete a final year project under the supervision of an industrial supervisor and a faculty member during the co-op. Students who are interested to take this course must obtain prior approval from the IMAC. For IIM students only. May be graded PP.
cilos: Integrate the knowledge they obtained from different courses.
Articulate the problem being solved and the solution effectively in writing and orally.
Cooperate with people from various disciplines and background.
Function effectively in multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary teams.
Manage the task assigned effectively by proper work allocation and personal arrangement.

IIMP 4980.title: Interdisciplinary Capstone Project I
IIMP 4980.description: Each IIM student is required to complete a capstone project before graduation. This is the first course of a two-term project in which the student can synthesize and apply skills and knowledge learnt from the program. The project is conducted under the supervision of the student’s Individualized Major Advisory Committee (IMAC). For IIM students only. Maybe graded PP.
cilos: Develop and integrate the knowledge in the students’ field of study.
Apply knowledge, tools and techniques learnt from the courses taken to a variety of tasks relevant to the students’ area of study.
Interpret and critically analyze data and draw conclusion from the information collected.
Analyze a problem and utilize the knowledge learnt to solve it.
Work independently and proactive in the execution of the tasks.
Present the related knowledge in written and oral format with rationale and logical organization effectively.
Self-evaluate their own learning progress and develop problem-solving skills.

IIMP 4990.title: Interdisciplinary Capstone Project II
IIMP 4990.description: Continuation of IIMP 4980. For IIM students only.
cilos: Develop and integrate the knowledge in the students’ field of study.

Interpret and critically analyze data and draw conclusion from the information collected.

Present the related knowledge in written and oral format with rationale and logical organization effectively.

IIMP 4991.title: Interdisciplinary Capstone Project
IIMP 4991.description: Each IIM student is required to complete a capstone project before graduation. This is a year-long project course which the student can synthesize and apply skills and knowledge learnt from the program. The project is conducted under the supervision of the student’s Individualized Major Advisory Committee (IMAC). Maybe graded PP. The credit load will be spread over the year. For students in Individualized Interdisciplinary Major (IIM).
cilos: Develop and integrate the knowledge in the students' field of study.
Apply knowledge, tools and techniques learnt from the courses taken to a variety of tasks relevant to the students' area of study.
Interpret and critically analyze data and draw conclusion from the information collected.
Analyze a problem and utilize the knowledge learnt to solve it.
Work independently and proactive in the execution of the tasks.
Present the related knowledge in written and oral format with rationale and logical organization effectively.
Self-evaluate their own learning progress and develop problem-solving skills.

IIMP 6050.title: Advanced Engineering Analysis
IIMP 6050.description: This course makes students acquainted with numerous quantitative measures to carry out practical quantitative analysis by applying to real-life challenges. It focuses on user-oriented and collaborative approach to guide students to acquire new tools and new knowledge by finishing several inspiring projects within course time. Students will have hands-on experience in quantitative analysis, user research, collaboration and project management. The course contains a number of different modules that are multidisciplinary and generally applicable to a high variety of problems. Enrolment in the course requires approval of the course instructor.
cilos: Comprehend and implement practical quantitative analysis tools.
Apply newly acquired tools, skills or knowledge to realistic situations.
Carry out firsthand and explicit multidisciplinary research.
Liaise and cooperate in team effectively.
Present ideas and results with clarity and efficiency.
Maintain organized documentation.

IIMP 6090.title: Postgraduate Seminar
IIMP 6090.description: Seminar topics presented by students, faculty and guest speakers. MPhil in Individualized Interdisciplinary Program (IIP) students must register and pass this course for one term before they graduate. PhD (IIP) students must register and pass this course for two terms before they graduate. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Understand current research trends and applications.
Demonstrate effective presentation skills in seminar presentations.
Gain insight into research on topics that are directly related to their own research.
Gain insight into research and research methodologies used by other scholars working on areas not directly related to their own focus area.

IIMP 6990.title: MPhil Thesis Research
IIMP 6990.description: Master's thesis is research supervised by a faculty member. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct a research proposal in their research area.

IIMP 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
IIMP 7990.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct a research proposal in their research area.
